config_name: Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 — Snapdragon X2 Elite, 32GB LPDDR5X, 1TB SSD, 14" 2.8K OLED 120Hz

battery.notes: 70Wh (VERIFIED). Same silicon as base; RAM tier does not change runtime materially.

price.notes: Base config VERIFIED at $1,399.99 ld+json; 32GB/1TB tier estimated +$300 CAD. Lenovo eCoupon pricing applies.

reviews.quote: The Yoga Slim 7x isn't just an alternative in ways that matter day-to-day. It's actually better. Lighter, brighter screen with actual black instead of gray, double the refresh rate, more keyboard travel, touchscreen if you want it. Same performance unplugged.
The new Lenovo Slim 7X, it's an awesome device this year. Super fast chip, crazy battery life.

praises: 32GB is the sweet spot — heavy Chrome/VS Code multitasking with no swap on the ARM side
2.8K 120Hz OLED with true blacks at ~1.24kg is best-in-class portability
Crazy battery life (Dave2D) — multi-day light use on 70Wh
Runs cool and near-silent under creator multitasking
Local AI features (Copilot+, Live Captions) run fully on-device via 80-TOPS NPU
complaints: ARM compatibility edge cases persist for niche pro apps and drivers
Integrated Adreno still not a gaming GPU
RAM soldered — buy the right tier up front
No Thunderbolt, no SD slot; dongle life for dock-heavy users
Base-tier 16GB upsell pressure: the config you want costs ~$300 more

design_philosophy: The volume config of Lenovo's Snapdragon flagship: X2 Elite + 32GB + 1TB on the 2.8K OLED 14-inch chassis — the version most reviewers actually recommend for creators and road warriors who prioritise battery and silence.
rating_notes: Inferred from same-line X2 Elite anchor (Rettinger/Dave2D quotes VERIFIED via lenovo.com/ca): 32GB vs 16GB → productivity +0.5, ai_ml +0.2 per NOTES convention. Non-touch tier → pen_touch 0.
